description: v0.4 candidate: string values containing U+0000. Each case is a scenario, not signed bytes. A "command" case: on a fresh host, a registered person sends the action with the given value in the given field and every other field valid; for record.append, the company has a policy granting that person write and a private structural profile whose schema is {note: string}. A "snapshot" case: a source company whose exported snapshot carries the given value at the given place (a source that admitted it before this rule) is staged and uploaded to a conforming destination, which then receives migration.ready. A host must give the expected outcome: "accept" (the command succeeds, or the destination answers ready), or a refusal with the given error code and HTTP status before anything is stored. A host that accepts a refused case, refuses an accepted one, or refuses with another code, is non-conforming. The rule is in spec/v0.4/SPEC.md section 2 (String values).
rule: A string value MUST NOT contain U+0000 (NUL), at any depth, in a command or in an imported snapshot. A host refuses such a command, and a destination refuses such a snapshot at migration.ready, with 400 nul_character. Every other character a JSON string can carry, other control characters included, is an ordinary value; the six-character text \u0000 is not U+0000.

cases.name: company name that is only U+0000
company name containing the six characters \u0000, not the character
record body string ending in U+0000
imported snapshot whose company name contains U+0000
imported snapshot whose company name contains U+0001
